title: Runlog rule pack (schema version 1)
description: A complete, self-contained description of a dice-driven creative-practice game. Packs are data, never code.

$schema.description: Path or URL to this schema, so your editor offers completions and validation.

schemaVersion.description: Major version of the pack contract. An engine that does not know this version refuses to load the pack rather than guessing at it.

id.description: Globally unique pack identifier in reverse-DNS form, e.g. com.example.my-game. Use a domain you control so two packs never collide in a player's library.

version.description: Version of this pack's content, e.g. 1.2.0.

description.description: One or two sentences on what the game is.

category.description: What kind of thing this is, in a word or two, for a catalog to group by: everyday, games, craft, fitness, cooking, writing…

tags.description: Free tags for a catalog to filter by: the game it is for, the hobby, the shape of play. Short, and in the words a person would search for.

requires.description: What a person needs before playing, shown in the catalog and the rulebook: the game and a system that runs it, mods or training packs, a wheel, a kitchen, supplies. Mark the ones that are nice to have `optional`; results can `need` those and be drawn again for a player who lacks them.

id.description: Unique among requirements. Table entries name it in `needs`.

label.description: What it is, in the words a person would use: Rocket League, a potter's wheel, an oven.

kind.description: What sort of thing it is, so a catalog can say 'needs a game' or 'needs equipment' at a glance.

optional.description: Nice to have rather than needed. A player says at the start whether they have it, and results that `need` it are drawn again when they do not.

note.description: A line on where to get it, which version, or what will do instead.

items.description: A physical or software requirement: the game and the system to play it on, a mod or training pack, a wheel, a kitchen, supplies.

id.description: The license, by SPDX identifier where one applies; `proprietary` or `custom` with the terms in `text`.

text.description: The license or notice in full, shown with the pack and printed in its rulebook. Required for `proprietary` and `custom`; welcome on any.

redistributable.description: Whether this pack's text may be included in exports meant for other people. When false the app shares roll results and references but never the rules prose, so a private transcription of a commercial rulebook stays private.

url.description: Where to obtain or license the original.

license.description: Licensing, and whether the app may share this pack's text.

capabilities.description: Engine features this pack needs. Declaring them lets an older app refuse the pack with a clear message instead of misplaying it.

items.description: An engine feature this pack needs in order to play correctly.

extends.description: Base pack this one layers on, for house rules and variants.

run.description: What one whole play session is called.

one.description: Singular, e.g. Room, Stage, Scene, Set.

unit.description: What one round of play is called.

one.description: Singular, e.g. Piece, Scene, Set, Track.

subject.description: What the thing produced in a unit is called.

finalize.description: Verb for closing a unit, e.g. Finalize, Fire, Commit.

terms.description: Overrides for other UI strings, keyed by the string's name.

vocabulary.description: The words this game uses. The interface speaks these rather than any built-in noun, which is what lets one engine host wholly different games.

unit.description: How units behave in this game.

clock.description: A clock every unit runs. A mode can set its own with `clock`.

kind.description: A stopwatch counts up from the start of the unit; a timer counts down from `minutes`.

minutes.description: How long a timer runs. Required for a timer; ignored by a stopwatch.

label.description: What the clock is called on screen. Defaults to the unit's name and number.

auto.description: Start it when the unit is entered and stop it when the unit closes. Off, the player starts it by hand; it still stops with the unit.

createsSubject.description: Whether entering a unit produces a new subject.

tables.description: Tables the game rolls on, keyed by id.

until.description: When the state lifts by itself. `unitEnd`: it is taken off everything it is on when the unit closes — a curse for this region, a cure for this region.

semantics.description: What this state means mechanically. Without it the engine would have to know what your state names mean, which is exactly what keeps an engine game-specific. `makesUntargetable` removes the subject from targeting; `excludesFromResult` leaves it in the run but out of the finished piece; `removesFromPlay` takes it out entirely.

group.description: States in the same group are mutually exclusive on one holder: applying one removes the others. Use it for outcomes that cannot both be true, like landed and missed.

additionalProperties.description: A persistent condition that sticks to a subject, or to the run, once applied.

notes.description: Reminders shown to the player in this mode.

issue.description: Marks this copy as issued to one person. Covered by the signature, so removing it invalidates that.
